subject: science
title: KS3 / Year 7-9 Science - Motion and Pressure
subtitle: Forces, speed, pressure, fluids, buoyancy, and practical investigation skills.
description: A KS3 physics revision pack about motion, speed, distance-time graphs, forces, pressure, fluids, density, upthrust, buoyancy, and practical investigation skills. The pack is source-faithful to the Motion and Pressure Study Pack and expands only where needed for clear curriculum practice.

data.title: Calculating Speed
data.instruction: Put the speed calculation steps in the correct order.
items: Write the equation speed = distance / time.
Substitute the distance and time values with units.
Divide the distance by the time.
Give the answer with a speed unit such as m/s.

data.title: Interpreting a Simple Journey Graph
data.instruction: Put the journey description in the correct order.
items: The pupil starts at the starting point.
The rising line shows the pupil walking away at constant speed.
The horizontal line shows the pupil stopping while time passes.
The steeper rising line shows the pupil moving away faster than before.

data.title: Forces During a Parachute Jump
data.instruction: Put the parachute jump force changes in the correct order.
items: At first, weight is greater than air resistance.
The parachutist accelerates downwards.
As speed increases, air resistance increases.
Air resistance balances weight, so the parachutist falls at constant speed.
The parachute opens and air resistance becomes much larger than weight.
The parachutist decelerates and may later reach a lower constant speed.

data.title: Pressure Investigation Method
data.instruction: Put the fair-test method in the correct order.
items: Place soft clay or sand on a flat bench.
Put the same block on its smallest face and add the same mass.
Leave the block for the same time each trial.
Remove the block and measure the depth of the mark.
Repeat three times and calculate a mean.
Repeat using larger contact areas while keeping the force the same.

data.title: Submarine Rising and Sinking
data.instruction: Put the ballast tank changes in the correct order for sinking then rising.
items: The ballast tanks fill with water.
The submarine mass and average density increase.
Weight becomes greater than upthrust, so the submarine sinks.
Compressed air pushes water out of the tanks.
Average density decreases.
Upthrust can become greater than weight, so the submarine rises.
